Question: If \(a\pm bi\) \((b\ne0)\) are imaginary roots of the equation \(x^3+qx+r=0,\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) \(q,\) and \(r\) are real numbers, then \(q\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\) is:
Solution:
Method 1: Compare imaginary parts

The constant \(r\) is real, so the imaginary part of the root equation can determine \(q\) without finding \(r\). Substitute the given root \(a+bi\), using \(i^2=-1\):
\[
\begin{aligned}
0&=(a+bi)^3+q(a+bi)+r\\
&=(a^3-3ab^2+qa+r)
+b(3a^2-b^2+q)i.
\end{aligned}
\]
A complex number equals zero only when both its real and imaginary parts are zero. Thus
\[
b(3a^2-b^2+q)=0.
\]
Since \(b\ne0\), division by \(b\) is valid and gives \(q=b^2-3a^2\), choice E.

Method 2: Use the missing quadratic coefficient

The two specified roots provide a quadratic factor. A root \(u\) gives a factor \(t-u\); because \(b\ne0\), the roots \(a+bi\) and \(a-bi\) are distinct, so both factors occur. Their product is
\[
(t-a-bi)(t-a+bi)=t^2-2at+a^2+b^2.
\]
The original cubic is monic, so its remaining factor is a monic linear expression \(t+s\). Therefore
\[
t^3+qt+r=(t^2-2at+a^2+b^2)(t+s).
\]
On the right, the coefficient of \(t^2\) is \(s-2a\). The original polynomial has no \(t^2\) term, so \(s=2a\). The coefficient of \(t\) is consequently
\[
q=(a^2+b^2)-2as
=a^2+b^2-4a^2
=b^2-3a^2.
\]
Thus the answer is choice E.
